# openCenter CLI

> openCenter CLI turns a declarative Kubernetes cluster configuration into validated GitOps assets and provider-specific lifecycle operations. It supports OpenStack, VMware, Baremetal, and Kind as the current infrastructure providers, with SOPS/Age secrets handling, Flux-oriented repository generation, import tooling, drift/backup operations, and resumable bootstrap.

This file is a concise navigation guide for code-oriented readers and language models. It is curated documentation, not an automatically generated artifact. Exact command flags belong to the command reference and generated per-command pages.

## Verified command capabilities

Use an explicit `organization/cluster` identifier where possible.

```bash
opencenter cluster init <name> --org <organization>
opencenter cluster configure <organization>/<cluster>
opencenter cluster validate <organization>/<cluster>
opencenter cluster doctor <organization>/<cluster>
opencenter cluster generate <organization>/<cluster>
opencenter cluster deploy <organization>/<cluster>
opencenter cluster destroy <organization>/<cluster>
```

Configuration and day-2 operations:

```bash
opencenter cluster list
opencenter cluster use <organization>/<cluster>
opencenter cluster active
opencenter cluster status <organization>/<cluster>
opencenter cluster describe <organization>/<cluster>
opencenter cluster set <organization>/<cluster> <path=value>...
opencenter cluster edit <organization>/<cluster>
opencenter cluster normalize <organization>/<cluster>
opencenter cluster export <organization>/<cluster>
opencenter cluster service enable <service>
opencenter cluster service disable <service>
opencenter cluster service status
opencenter cluster service options <service>
opencenter cluster pool add <pool>
opencenter cluster pool update <pool>
opencenter cluster pool scale <pool>
opencenter cluster pool remove <pool>
opencenter cluster pool list
opencenter cluster drift detect <organization>/<cluster>
opencenter cluster drift reconcile <organization>/<cluster>
opencenter cluster drift schedule <organization>/<cluster>
opencenter cluster backup create <organization>/<cluster>
opencenter cluster backup list <organization>/<cluster>
opencenter cluster backup restore <backup-id>
opencenter cluster backup delete <backup-id>
opencenter cluster backup schedule <organization>/<cluster>
opencenter cluster lock <organization>/<cluster>
opencenter cluster unlock <organization>/<cluster>
opencenter cluster import scan --repo-path <path>
opencenter cluster import report
opencenter cluster import apply
opencenter cluster migrate-layout --org <organization>
opencenter cluster sync openstack <organization>/<cluster>
```

Secrets are split between backend CRUD, manifest synchronization, and SOPS/Age file operations:

```bash
opencenter secrets login
opencenter secrets list
opencenter secrets describe <name>
opencenter secrets get <name>
opencenter secrets set <name>
opencenter secrets delete <name>
opencenter secrets sync <organization>/<cluster>
opencenter secrets validate <organization>/<cluster>
opencenter secrets encrypt
opencenter secrets decrypt
opencenter secrets status
opencenter secrets keys generate
opencenter secrets keys rotate
opencenter secrets keys backup
opencenter secrets keys validate
opencenter secrets keys check
opencenter secrets keys revoke
opencenter secrets keys reconcile
opencenter secrets keys set-primary
```

Other built-in groups are `settings`, `plugins list`, `version`, and `shell-init`; standard Cobra `help` and `completion` are also available.

## Runtime and generation facts

- `main.go` calls `cmd.ExecuteWithContext`; the canonical production dependency graph is `di.NewApp` in `internal/di/app.go`, adapted for compatibility with `di.NewAppContainer`.
- `cmd.NewBuiltinRootCmd` creates the deterministic built-in Cobra tree. External `opencenter-*` executables are discovered and attached only after built-ins in the production runtime, using `OPENCENTER_PLUGINS_DIR`, `<config-dir>/plugins`, and `PATH`.
- The tools-tagged command-reference generator receives `cmd.NewBuiltinRootCmd()`, so generated Cobra reference pages cover built-ins only and never load external plugins.
- `cluster generate` runs `internal/cluster.SetupService`: config load, `CopyBase`, encrypted application render/promotion, infrastructure render, Flux bridge render, and optional non-Kind OpenTofu provisioning. `PipelineGenerator` is a supporting API, not the live top-level path.
- Rendering uses descriptor coverage, an immutable built-in `RenderCatalog`, owned action validation, atomic workspace writes, and promotion that preserves `custom/`.
- `internal/secretartifacts` maps logical secret owners to deterministic physical artifacts. `internal/secrets` performs locked transactional manifest sync with encryption, journaling/rollback, ownership hashes, and state. SOPS overlay value encryption is a separate `internal/sops` concern.
- OpenStack, VMware, Baremetal, and Kind are the current infrastructure provider paths. AWS, GCP, and Azure are rejected planned/unavailable providers.
